title: Learn from examples
summary: Machine learning uses examples to choose a rule or model. A model is a stored way to make predictions. A prediction is an estimate, not a known fact.
introduction: Machine learning uses examples to choose a rule or model. A model is a stored way to make predictions. A prediction is an estimate, not a known fact. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Machine learning uses examples to choose a rule or model. A model is a stored way to make predictions. A prediction is an estimate, not a known fact.

blocks.title: Before you start
blocks.text: The Python examples need a separate Python 3 environment. They use built-in tools, not a paid AI service. These small demonstrations do not make reliable real-world predictions.
This course teaches the basics. It does not cover every feature of Machine Learning. Keep real personal data and secret keys out of practice files.

blocks.title: Learn from examples

blocks.text: Each pair connects a page count to fictional reading minutes. The pattern suggests twice as many minutes as pages, but three examples are not proof.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Add the pair (4, 8) and explain its meaning.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not say that every learner reads at the same speed.
For more detail later, use this [Machine Learning further reading](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course).
